question: W-60: are the four Mekanism modules loadable together, and is the earlier 'mekanism:security is not bound' failure a port defect or a development-environment artifact?
answer: There is no production defect. The three addon mods load beside the core in a clean remapped release server; only Loom development runs cannot host them beside the core because each mod source set lives in its own Fabric class-path group, so addon code resolves a second copy of the core registry statics.

development_attempts.configuration: remapped addon release JARs copied into a development run's mods/ directory
observed: IllegalStateException: Registry value mekanism:security is not bound
development_attempts.explanation: The release JARs are remapped to intermediary names; Loom development runs use named mappings, so addon code cannot bind to Minecraft or to the named core.

development_attempts.configuration: addon source-set outputs appended to the named development classpath of runHandshakeServer
observed: 48 mods load (core plus all three addons); tools and additions initialize
generators fails in GeneratorsBlocks with 'Registry value mekanism:security is not bound' in 3 of 4 attempts
one attempt started the server normally ('Done (6.204s)'), so the failure is non-deterministic
development_attempts.explanation: The same class files are reachable both from Loom's per-source-set class-path groups and from the plain development classpath, so core registry statics may be initialized twice. A diagnostic build recorded the binding of mekanism:security in one FabricDeferredHolder copy and an unbound holder in another copy.

development_attempts.configuration: named (non-remapped) dev JARs from build/{tools,additions,generators}-devlibs copied into a development run's mods/ directory
observed: 48 mods load; tools and additions initialize
generators fails with the same 'Registry value mekanism:security is not bound'
development_attempts.explanation: JARs loaded from mods/ are resolved outside the core's class-path group, so they again see a second copy of the core statics. Named mappings remove the BlockGlowPanel failure but not the duplication.

release_check.server: clean fabric-server-launch.jar with fabric-api, team_reborn_energy and the four remapped Mekanism JARs
release_check.development_vs_release_delta: Core SERVER snapshots are 304 values in a development world and 303 in a release world: general.alphaWarning exists only in the development schema (FabricServerConfig sanitizes it for release). The earlier planning figure 459 assumed the development core count (304 + 63 + 41 + 51); the release total is 458.

consequence: fabric-paired-network-smoke.sh and fabric-configuration-rejection-smoke.sh stay core-only development runs and assert the core 304-value server snapshot; they no longer install addon JARs.
fabric-packaged-smoke.sh remains the four-module release check and asserts the complete release schema snapshot (configs=10 values=458).
